newsitem.title: UK: Patten asks why democracy came late to HK - paper.
newsitem.headline: Patten asks why democracy came late to HK - paper.

text.p: Hong Kong's last British governor, Chris Patten, believes future historians will ask why democratic institutions were not introduced to the colony much earlier, the Times reported on Friday.
Patten told the newspaper it would have been impossible in the 1950s and 1960s because of the waves of refugees arriving in the colony, which reverts to Chinese control in just three days.
The main task at that time was to find a home for these people, but by the 1970s most in Hong Kong had been born there, the Times reported Patten as saying.
And Patten also said claims that Hong Kong people did not care for democracy was an untrue justification for the delay in introducing liberal reform.
"There was also a patronising and rather racist view that people would not be able to handle democratic development, it would be bad for economic development," he told the paper.
"In fact, far from being bad for economic development, democracy has been an astonishing success," Patten added.
